question: Refer to the exhibit. The MDS-EDGE-Switch and MDS-Core-Switch are configured with NPV and NPIV features. The FLOGI from Cisco UCS is received by the MDS-Core-Switch on interface fc1/2. An engineer tried to move all traffic between the MDS-EDGE-Switch and MDS-Core-Switch from interface fc1/2 to fc1/3, but the attempt failed. Which set of actions completes the configuration?
context:
Topology: UCS Server -fc1/1- MDS-EDGE-Switch -fc1/2, fc1/3- MDS-Core-Switch (-fc1/2, fc1/3).
MDS-EDGE-SWITCH(config)# npv traffic-map server-interface fc1/1 external-interface fc1/3
fc1/1: External interface list should contain the one in use
imageNote: Diagram: UCS Server connects via fc1/1 to MDS-EDGE-Switch, which connects via fc1/2 and fc1/3 to MDS-Core-Switch.
options: Shut down fc1/1 in the MDS-EDGE-Switch. Re-apply the command. Enable interface fc1/1.
Disable the NPIV feature in the MDS-EDGE-Switch. Re-enable the NPIV feature. Disable interface fc1/3.
Disable the NPIV feature in the MDS-EDGE-Switch. Re-enable the NPV feature. Disable interface fc1/1.
Shutdown fc1/3 in the MDS-EDGE-Switch. Re-apply the command. Enable interface fc1/3.
theory: NPV's 'npv traffic-map server-interface ... external-interface ...' command pins a server-facing interface to a specific NP uplink, but NX-OS only accepts the mapping if the external interface list for that server interface currently includes the uplink already in active use - you cannot directly retarget a live, logged-in server interface to a different external interface. The workaround is to shut the server interface down first (forcing its devices to log out and clearing the active mapping), reapply the traffic-map command so the new external interface is accepted, and then re-enable the server interface so devices log back in over the newly mapped uplink. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 8 - NPIV and NPV)
